newsitem.title: UK: Softs Outlook - Cocoa to rebound, sugar lingers.
newsitem.headline: Softs Outlook - Cocoa to rebound, sugar lingers.

text.p: Cocoa futures may regain some ground on bargain-hunting this week after Thursday's fund-led sell-off wiped nearly 100 stg off values in a day following a three-week rally, traders said on Monday.

While September cocoa might find some comfort above 1,000 stg a tonne, the lows seen on Thursday, the market could struggle to re-conquer the 1,100 resistance, which until Thursday's reversal was a major chart support.
Elsewhere, white sugar might linger above its immediate floor.
Robusta coffee could attempt to push higher and break out of a tight range, but might not have enough upside momentum to sustain a rise.
Fundamentally, coffee looked vulnerable to a downside move in the face of weak supply/demand indicators.
So far the Brazilian winter had been mild and no crop-damaging frosts were forecast for the coming weeks.
London's September coffee is locked in a triangle chart formation with initial support pegged at $1,750 and resistance at $1,990. It closed Friday unchanged at $1,795 a tonne.

But traders said nearby green coffee stocks held by manufacturers and traders were building up as demand for finished coffee continued to slide, possibility due to the effects of recent increase in retail prices.
But London might draw some strength from the lack of origin sales, noticeably from key producer Indonesia.
Local Indonesian prices stayed firm on short covering by shippers, despite higher arrivals. Traders said growers were selling coffee to raise cash ahead of the start of the new school year
Cocoa prices recovered slightly to end Friday 20 up at 1,039 stg and compared with the lows of 1,000 seen a day before.
Traders said European manufacturers were likely to be tempted by the lower levels even if sterling strengthened against major European units.
"Current levels are quite cheap compared with 1,165 or 1,170 seen earlier last week," said one French trader.
"The market is now back to where it started in early June," he said. Cocoa's frenetic rally had been mostly fuelled by aggressive fund buying.

The funds were estimated to have held some 16,000 lots in long positions as of Wednesday last week. By the end of business on Thursday, the open position in September stood at 23,721 lots, down by a hefty 12,636.
The rally that had hoisted prices to one-year highs seemed overdone. It was purely speculative involvement, with the industry reluctant to ride on the booming prices.

Manufacturers were looking for a definite clue on the size of the coming West Africa crops before dabbling in the futures market. But traders said it would take four to eight weeks before reliable crop estimates were made available.
In white sugar, the approaching expiry of the spot August contract should occupy most trading interest in London, although earlier perceptions of seasonal physical tightness seemed to have changed.

Traders said the nearby spread would also be closely watched as August positions were rolled forward before the July 16 expiry. As usual, a hefty number of against actuals and crossed trades were expected.
Aug/Oct would probably widen as outright August firmed on account of widespread but as yet unconfirmed talk of untenderable sugars hedged against August by the trade.
"Whether they are there or whether they're just being talked about, we don't know," said one trader.
The spread saw choppy movement last week, narrowing to under $3 at one stage but then moving back out again nearer to $5.

Technical analysts said August's move below $320 suggested prices might again challenge support at around $315.50, at the upward trendline extending from January's low of $295.00. It closed Friday 70 cents down at $319.20. -- London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
